source_title: The Effect of Temperature and Milling Process on Steel Scale Utilized as a Pigment for Ceramic Glaze

issues.issue: Suspension quantity is rendered as 1.355-1.400 g/L. Do not reinterpret separators or convert to density without checking original presentation and intent.
Discussion describes matte-to-gloss change at 900 C; conclusions describe matte appearance at 800 and 900 C. Do not emit an unambiguous surface label without specimen/figure review.
Below-detection values and dashes are not zero. Fe reported as Fe2O3 equivalent is not proof all iron is hematite; XRD reports several iron phases.
N2 is reported for TG/DTA. Do not copy that atmosphere into glaze firing records; processes are distinct.

model_implications: Keep particle-size distribution and milling/calcination history alongside oxide chemistry.
Separate additive mass basis, application method and firing program for each specimen.
Reported absence of visible defects is not a zero failure probability or food-contact safety result.
